name: Bouillotte
description: Bouillotte is a historic 18th-century French gambling game that represents a critical evolution in the history of Poker. Emerging during the French Revolution as a derivative of Brelan, it is a fast-paced vying game for 3-5 players. It is unique for its use of a stripped pack and a 'retourné' (turned card) that can complete a player's Brelan into a Brelan Carré (four-of-a-kind). It famously introduced the concept of the 'Cave' (fixed chip stack), which restricted betting to the chips currently on the table.

history.origins: Bouillotte was developed in late 18th-century France as a modification of Brelan to regulate betting behavior during the volatile Revolutionary period. It became so popular that it influenced the development of early American Stud Poker.
timeline: 1789: Bouillotte gains popularity in Parisian gambling dens.
1830s: Featured prominently in the literature of Balzac and Thackeray.
1870s: Replaced by modern Poker in international gambling circles.
Present: A rare historical game studied for its influence on the betting structures of modern gambling.
history.cultural: Regarded as the 'Enlightenment Game', its rules on the 'Cave' were a precursor to modern 'Table Stakes' in casino poker.
history.evolution: The game moved from the simple 3-card vying of Brelan to a format where a community card (the retourné) added a dramatic fifth card to the potential combinations.

setup.players: 4 players are standard (using 20 cards). 3 players remove Queens (16 cards). 5 players add Jacks (24 cards).
setup.deck: A stripped piquet pack: Ace, King, Queen, 9, 8 in each suit. Ranking: A-K-Q-9-8.
setup.dealing: Players ante into the pot. Dealer deals 3 cards to each player and turns the next card face-up (the retourné).

rules.objective: Win the pot by holding the highest hand or by forcing all other players to fold during the vying rounds.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Ante**: Each player puts a fixed amount in the pot. 2. **Deal**: Players receive 3 cards and see the retourné. 3. **Vying**: Starting left of dealer, players bet, call, or fold. 4. **Showdown**: Best hand wins. Hand hierarchy: Brelan Carré (four of a kind using retourné), Brelan Favori (three of a kind including retourné), simple Brelan (three of a kind), then highest point-total in a suit.
keyRules: The 'Cave' rule: You cannot bet more than the chips you have on the table.
If no Brelan is held, the player with the highest total value in a single suit wins.
Aces are worth 11, face cards 10, others face value.

strategy.basic: Only bet aggressively if you hold a pair that matches the retourné, as this guaranteed a Brelan Favori.
strategy.intermediate: Pot Odds: Calculate the total chips in the pot versus your remaining Cave. If you are 'Pot Committed', folding becomes mathematically incorrect.
strategy.advanced: Bluffing on Suit Totals: Since a Brelan is rare, most pots are won on suit totals. If the retourné is an Ace, bluffing that you have high cards in that suit is a standard tactic.
tips: Manage your Cave carefully; losing it all means you must buy back in or exit.
Pay close attention to the retourné—it is the most important card on the table.

variations.name: Brelan (Parent Game)
variations.description: The older version without the retourné card; play is purely based on the 3-card hand.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Listed to document Bouillotte's parent game; no separate engine overrides are modeled for Brelan.

scoring.winCondition: Best hand at showdown or all opponents fold.

synthesis.shortDescription: The precursor to American stud poker. A high-speed vying game from the French Revolution where a single turned card can turn a simple pair into a legendary Brelan Carré. Manage your Cave, read your rivals, and master the art of the Enlightenment bluff.
